_comment: The reading-SELECTION baseline -- a SEPARATE experiment from the parse baseline (baseline.json). The parse baseline gates the GRAMMAR + lexicon: what forest is produced (the pins ask whether the correct STRUCTURE survives). THIS file gates the RANKER: which reading gets chosen from that forest, scored READING-level (structure + word senses) against the adjudication ledger. Different re-baselining triggers: grammar work re-draws the parse baseline without touching this file; a new selection draw, a prompt change, or a ledger revision re-derives THIS baseline without touching the parse numbers. Update deliberately, never to make a red run go green.

provenance.forest: ranks experiments/parsing/ranks/2026-09-29-d95-quantities.json, RE-RECORDED live on this snapshot — the prior draw (2026-08-22-productiontrace) keys by sentence text and sentence splitting changed

gates.reading_unadjudicated: GATED: must be 0 on the tracked replay -- an unadjudicated decision makes the number a partial count, not a measurement; a new draw choosing novel readings fails until its ledger rows are adjudicated (mirrors audit-skeletons).
gates.invalid_selected: GATED: must be 0 (SELECTION-VALIDITY). The ranker has no kernel veto -- every candidate type-checks -- so the ledger and this validity check are its controls.
gates.structure_correct: diagnostic only -- reported, never gated; the pins belong to the parse baseline's faithfulness gate.

_provenance_note_2026-08-22b-production-: RE-MEASURED after the #210/#205 close-out (2026-08-22, commit a05cfa1, snapshot wordnet-umls-aligned-2026-08-22c). Tracked draw: ranks/2026-08-22-productiontrace.json, selections/2026-08-22-productiontrace-live.json. Live and replay AGREE. Coverage: grammar-gap 0, expected-hits 62/62, miss-set unchanged, skeletons 170 (unchanged). Selection: 41 eligible, 30 correct, 0 unadjudicated, 0 invalid-selected — reading-correct 30/40 -> 30/41, holds. total-readings 613 -> 674, ungated and inside the 700 ceiling. ONE ADJUDICATION was needed to reach 0 unadjudicated: «The MSI relationship compared favourably…» chose a reading structurally IDENTICAL to two rows already ruled `wrong` for that unit (the conjunction split, hanging «for vulnerabilities» on the subject), and wrong on both contested sense axes besides. Recorded `wrong`. METHOD, after getting it wrong earlier the same day: a single live run is a DRAW, not a measurement. Draw until clean (up to 3), PROMOTE the clean draw to ranks/, replay it to confirm live and replay agree, and only then read the numbers. Four earlier draws that day reported 61 hits twice on DIFFERENT sentences; two of them carried malformed sense-ranker replies (eigenius#212), and none had been promoted. Check `grep -c 'malformed reply'` before attributing any delta to code.
_provenance_note_2026-09-29: The eligible set grew 40 -> 41 because one unit stopped being single-reading (baseline.json encoded 2 -> 1), which makes it ambiguous and therefore a decision the ranker has to take. That happened in SEPTEMBER, not at this commit: the 2026-09-09 run already recorded reading-correct 30/41. reading_correct is unchanged at 30 and reading_unadjudicated is 0, so the extra decision was already adjudicated — the ranker is choosing on one more unit and getting the same number right, which is a wider denominator rather than a regression.
_provenance_note_2026-09-29-d95-quantiti: Every gated figure holds across the quantity work: eligible 41, chose 41, reading-correct 30, reading-unadjudicated 0, invalid-selected 0, structure-correct 33. The one decision this run left unadjudicated was adjudicated WRONG (the MSI-relationship PP attachment; see baseline.json's note and eigenius#264), which moved it from unadjudicated to wrong and left reading-correct at 30 — the ranker is choosing on the same number of units and getting the same number right.
_provenance_note_2026-09-29-d95-slices-6: D95 SLICES 6-8 — MEASURED, NOT ADOPTED: `provenance` and `expected` above still describe the 2026-09-29-d95-quantities draw, pending the maintainer's ruling on reading_correct. The tracked draw for the slice 6-8 forest is selections/2026-09-29-d95-slice8.json over ranks/2026-09-29-d95-slice8.json (snapshot wordnet-umls-aligned-2026-09-29-quantities-s8b, commit 7df7bce): recorded live, 0 malformed replies, and replayed with 41 hits and 0 misses. A new draw was required: slices 7a and 7d changed the candidate pools of four eligible units, and the selection key includes the glosses of the page's earlier selections (reading_ranker.rs, selection_key), so with the page's first unit among the four no later key of the old recording can match. It scores reading-correct 29/41 against the expected 30, wrong 12, unadjudicated 0 (six ledger rows added), invalid-selected 0, structure-correct 34 (33). The decisions that changed, on the four new pools: «The four other RecQ DNA helicases …» wrong -> correct (`the four` takes `four` out of the compound, so the UMLS qualifier-junk nouns for `other` are no longer offered); «Synthetic lethality is an interaction between two genetic events.» correct -> wrong (`genetic` a02734192, the sense the ledger already ruled wrong for this sentence in an earlier draw); «We analysed two …» wrong -> wrong; «We identified three …» correct -> correct. On pools identical to the old draw's: «Many cancers exhibit an impairment of a DNA repair pathway.» and «Some cancers do not respond to immune checkpoint blockade.» correct -> wrong, «The use of immune checkpoint blockade can be limited by toxicity.» wrong -> correct. Those pools did not change, but each decision's prompt carries the page's earlier selections (resolver_llm.rs), and «Synthetic lethality …», whose selection changed, is the page's first unit. Net 30 + 1 - 1 - 1 = 29. Lowering expected.reading_correct to 29, or drawing again, is the maintainer's decision.
